title: Initiative plug-in manifest (the 'definition' body)
description: What a plug-in declares it can do. A plug-in is a container, which names its `service` and answers Initiative's calls, or declarative, which names its `hosts` and no service, and whose endpoints, connection checks, webhook events, schedules and actions Initiative runs itself from the requests and JSONata expressions written here, keeping the values they write on items; one plug-in is never both. This is the 'definition' field of the document served at /.well-known/initiative-plugin.json, NOT that whole document: a registrar also requires protocol_version, public_id and kind alongside it, and refuses a definition served bare. Generated from the platform's own validator vocabulary. A manifest that satisfies this schema is well-formed, not necessarily acceptable. Cross-references (the endpoint a widget binds, a requires term's connection, an endpoint's service prefix), the direction-specific rules on an endpoint, the features/blocks cross-check in both directions, UTF-8 byte-size caps, the rules tying a connection's flow and token to its scope and fields, what a webhooks block names, what a vendor setup writes to, whether every expression parses, what a declarative request and its steps name, the bounds, ids and endpoints of schedules, which terms each kind's schedules, actions, fields and webhook events take, the unique keys and ids of fields, parts, actions and settings, what a part's nodes, a field's element actions and an action's endpoint and params name, the placeholders in a part's text, and a part's size and depth are enforced by the platform on publish and are not expressible here.

plugin_kind.description: The kind every plug-in manifest has, container or declarative: a declarative plug-in is one with no 'service' block.

public_id.description: '<publisher>.<slug>'. The name the deployment's registration is matched by, and the namespace this plug-in's events are emitted under.

scopes.description: The scopes this plug-in asks a community to grant: what its installation and member tokens act with. The fixed scopes, and 'plugins:<public_id>' for each plug-in this one uses, to call its public endpoints and read the values it shows on items (at most 24 of those). The community grants some or all of them when it installs the plug-in, and a token never carries more than was granted. Writing implies reading. Absent means none.

calls_plugins.description: This plug-in may act through any plug-in the community lets it use, not only those its scopes name as 'plugins:<public_id>'. When a community installs another plug-in, it is asked there whether this one may use it, which grants 'plugins:<public_id>' for it. Absent: only the plug-ins its scopes name.

service.description: A container plug-in's service, which Initiative calls. Absent for a declarative plug-in, whose public id is its listing's.

features.description: What this plug-in contributes. Cross-checked against the blocks present in both directions: a feature with no block, or a block with no feature, is refused.

minimum_age.description: How old somebody must be to use this plug-in, by where they are. Keys are ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes, upper case, and 'default' for every country not listed: {"default": 16, "US": 13}. The age of digital consent differs by country, inside the EU as well as outside it, which is why a region is a country rather than a regime. Absent, or a country with no entry and no 'default': the deployment's own minimum applies. A declaration, not a gate: whether a deployment enforces it, and how it learns somebody's age and country, are its decisions. At most 64 entries, each from 13 to 21.

min_plugin_api.description: The oldest plug-in API contract this plug-in needs, as 'MAJOR.MINOR': '4.1'. The contract is the plug-in API published with initiative-plugin-sdk, versioned as that package is. A deployment serving contract S can run it when S has the same major version and a minor version at least this one's. Absent: any contract; the plug-in makes no claim. Beside a listing's min_app_version, the oldest Initiative release it runs on, this says what the plug-in calls rather than which release serves it.

hosts.description: Declarative plug-ins, which must name at least one: every host their requests, paging and links may reach. A container plug-in names none.

scopes.description: Declarative plug-ins: the scopes this plug-in asks a community to grant, all of them read scopes ('<resource>:read'). A declarative plug-in keeps its own values on items it can read and does not call Initiative, and Initiative keeps them only on items these scopes read. A container plug-in declares its scopes in its service block.

schedules.description: What Initiative runs on an interval for each community: a container plug-in's schedule hook, or a declarative plug-in's read and the values it writes from the answer. At most 8.

community_summary.description: A read endpoint whose declared returns describe this community's standing with your service — what it has used, what it is allowed. A deployment may render them on the community's own settings page, beside its own figures. Whether it does is the deployment's decision and not this manifest's: a plug-in the operator did not ship is declaring where it would like to appear, which is not the same as appearing.

dashboards.description: Ready-made arrangements of this plug-in's own widgets. Publishing the plug-in publishes one ordinary dashboard listing per entry, offered to communities that install the plug-in.

fields.description: How the plug-in's values on items are shown there. Any plug-in may keep values on items: a container writes them with its installation token, and for a declarative plug-in Initiative writes them from the plug-in's expressions.

parts.description: Pieces of items' pages and views, built from Initiative's components and bound to the plug-in's fields and actions.

actions.description: What a reader may run on an item: a container plug-in's write endpoints, which its handlers answer, or a declarative plug-in's calls and changes to its values, which Initiative makes.

settings.description: Values the community's admins set on the install, which the plug-in's expressions and its parts' text read. At most 16.

help.description: Help with the plug-in, keyed by language tag: markdown of at most 2000 characters in each language. Initiative shows it behind a '?' on the headers of the plug-in's parts and on its settings, in the reader's language, or failing that in any.

path.description: A route on the plug-in's own service, never an address. The deployment joins it to the base URL its registration supplies.

localizedText.description: Localized text, keyed by language tag. At least one usable entry; the platform falls back to the reader's language, then to any entry. Values should be strings: text longer than 120 characters is truncated, and an entry that is not a string, is not a language tag, or falls past the first 40 is ignored rather than refused.

requires.description: Connection ids that must hold a value before this is offered. Exactly one of 'all_of' or 'any_of'; each id must name a connection this manifest declares. Absent means always available.

accessHint.description: What the credential will be used for. Display-only: it is shown beside the form so an admin can mint a minimal credential, and no other system's permissions are enforced from it.

managed.description: Returned by the plug-in's after_connect hook when a flow finishes; it is not typed into the settings form.

vendor.description: What an operator supplies once per deployment for the vendor's own client: its id, its secret, its signing key. Declared here and never valued here: the values are entered on the deployment, or written there by the vendor's own setup flow, and referenced from a connection's flow or token as '{vendor.<key>}'.

label.description: What the vendor client is called, for the operator's form.

setup.description: How the vendor's client can be made for a deployment by the vendor itself, rather than registered by hand. Absent: the operator enters every value.

type.description: A 'secret' is written once and never shown again.

required.description: The plug-in is not live on a deployment until every required value is set.

vendorSetup.description: A flow at the vendor that creates the vendor's client and answers with its values. Initiative runs it from the operator's browser and writes what the vendor answers into the deployment's vendor values, so none is typed or copied. One member per flow, told apart by 'kind'.

githubAppManifestSetup.description: A GitHub App created from a manifest (GitHub's app manifest flow). The operator confirms it on GitHub, and Initiative exchanges the code GitHub returns for the new app's values. Initiative fills in every address itself (the callback, setup, webhook and redirect URLs), so the manifest names none.

values.description: Which vendor value each of GitHub's answers is written to: one of this plug-in's vendor field keys to one field of GitHub's manifest-conversion response. Every key must be a field of the vendor block, each response field is written at most once, and 'client_secret', 'pem' and 'webhook_secret' are written only to a 'secret' field.

githubAppManifest.description: What GitHub is asked to create: the parts of a GitHub App manifest a plug-in decides.

name.description: The name GitHub offers for the new app. The operator may change it on GitHub, where an app's name is unique.

public.description: Any GitHub account may install the new app. Absent: only the account that owns it.

default_permissions.description: The permissions the app is created with, by GitHub's name for each, such as 'issues'. At most 100.

default_events.description: The webhook events the app subscribes to, by GitHub's name for each, such as 'issues'. GitHub accepts an event only beside a permission that covers it. At most 100.

options.description: Required when type is 'select'. The values themselves — a consumer that shows a menu writes its own words for them.

options_from.description: Where this parameter's values come from when only the plug-in can know them. Names a read endpoint in THIS manifest and which of its returns holds the values; a consumer building a form asks the deployment to resolve it rather than showing a text box. For everything a manifest cannot list because the answer differs per install and changes after it — a repository, a channel, a board, a project. `options` is the other case: a set that is the same on every deployment forever. Declaring values, not a control: what to draw is still the consumer's. Resolution is server-side, inherits the source endpoint's `requires` and `cache_ttl_seconds`, and a source that cannot be resolved leaves the parameter enterable rather than unusable.

endpoint.description: A read endpoint this same manifest declares. Not another plug-in's: reading across plug-ins has no consent story, and an id from elsewhere is refused on publish.

key.description: Which of that endpoint's returns holds the values. Must be one it declares, and a list: a menu comes from a column of values, not from one.

label_key.description: Optional. A second return, parallel to `key`, holding what a person reads — a board's title beside its opaque id. Absent means the value is its own label.

needs.description: Optional. What to send that endpoint, written as one of ITS parameter names to one of THIS endpoint's. A repository's labels, a board's fields, a field's values — past the first source in a form, most of them answer differently depending on what has been chosen already, and a source that could not be told a sibling's answer could only ever offer the whole account's worth. Every named sibling must be a parameter this endpoint declares, and none of them this one. Until all of them have a value the source is not called and the parameter stays enterable, exactly as for a source that will not resolve.

list.description: Several values rather than one. Cardinality is a fact about the value, so it is yours; what to draw for it is the consumer's. Without it, a plug-in wanting several of something declares a string and documents a comma — which nothing downstream can validate or complete.

type.description: The parameter vocabulary minus 'select', because a select is a control and the value behind one is a string.

list.description: Several values rather than one. It matters to a consumer with somewhere to put exactly one — a form field, a tile's number — which is why it is a flag rather than a second set of types.

of.description: Another return of this same endpoint that this one is counted against: 'used' of 'allowed', so a consumer can draw the pair as one measure. Both must be single 'int' returns, and a return is never counted against itself. The other return answering null means there is no ceiling, and the figure stands alone. Absent: a figure in its own right — a balance, a tally, a date it resets.

scope.description: Who the credential belongs to. 'static' is one credential the whole community uses; 'interactive' is each member's own account at a vendor that authorizes people. It does not say how the credential is obtained: a static connection with a 'flow' is still one credential for the whole community, run by an admin through the vendor's own pages rather than typed into a form. An interactive connection always declares a 'flow'.

fields.description: Without a 'flow', what an admin types. With one, only the values the plug-in's after_connect hook returns, and every field is 'managed'. The tokens a flow obtains are held apart from these, under reserved keys the plug-in never declares.

flow.description: How the connection is established. Initiative runs it: the redirect, the code exchange, refreshing and revoking. The plug-in never holds the vendor client's secret or a refresh token.

token.description: How a usable access token is got for this connection. Absent: the tokens the flow stored, refreshed as needed. Static connections only.

connectionFlow.description: An OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow (RFC 6749 §4.1) that Initiative runs for a connection, with the redirect addresses the deployment publishes.

authorize_url.description: The vendor's authorization endpoint, https. May name a vendor value as '{vendor.<key>}' and one of this connection's own fields as '{<key>}'.

token_url.description: The vendor's token endpoint, https. May name a vendor value as '{vendor.<key>}' and one of this connection's own fields as '{<key>}'.

client_id.description: The vendor client's id, normally '{vendor.client_id}'. May name a vendor value as '{vendor.<key>}' and one of this connection's own fields as '{<key>}'.

client_secret.description: The vendor client's secret, normally '{vendor.client_secret}'. Absent for a public client. May name a vendor value as '{vendor.<key>}' and one of this connection's own fields as '{<key>}'.

scopes.description: The vendor scopes asked for, sent space-separated.

authorize_params.description: Extra query parameters for the authorization request. May name a vendor value as '{vendor.<key>}' and one of this connection's own fields as '{<key>}'.

install_url.description: Static connections only. The vendor's install page, for a connection an organization installs: the person installs first, the vendor returns to the setup address with the installation's id, and one authorization trip follows so the plug-in can check who installed it. Requires 'after_connect'. May name a vendor value as '{vendor.<key>}' and one of this connection's own fields as '{<key>}'.

after_connect.description: What runs once the code is exchanged, with the fresh access token, to learn the connection's managed values and an account label, or to refuse it. A container plug-in sets true, and Initiative calls its after_connect hook; a declarative plug-in gives the call and its mapping.

revoke.description: How a grant is ended at the vendor when the connection ends: 'rfc7009' posts to 'revoke_url' with the client's credentials; 'github_grant' sends DELETE to 'revoke_url' (GitHub's 'Delete an app authorization') with the client's credentials as HTTP Basic auth and the access token in the JSON body as 'access_token'; 'hook' calls the plug-in's revoke hook with the tokens, so a container plug-in's only. Absent: the tokens are deleted and nothing is sent.

revoke_url.description: The vendor's revocation endpoint: RFC 7009's for 'rfc7009', or GitHub's grant address (https://api.github.com/applications/{vendor.client_id}/grant) for 'github_grant'. Required when 'revoke' is either. May name a vendor value as '{vendor.<key>}' and one of this connection's own fields as '{<key>}'.

connectionToken.description: An access token minted on demand rather than stored: Initiative signs a JWT with the vendor key and exchanges it, and caches the answer until shortly before it expires.

exchange_url.description: Where the signed JWT is posted, https. The answer's 'token' (or 'access_token') and 'expires_at' (or 'expires_in') are read. May name a vendor value as '{vendor.<key>}' and one of this connection's own fields as '{<key>}'.

exchange_body.description: A JSON body posted with the signed JWT, such as the narrower permissions a token is asked for. Absent: none. A string anywhere in it may name a vendor value as '{vendor.<key>}' and one of this connection's own fields as '{<key>}'. Or an expression answering the body, which reads only 'connection': this connection's own non-secret fields by key, its managed values included, as 'after_connect' stored them. A body that names a vendor value is written as an object. An answer that is not an object fails the token request, so the connection cannot be used until the expression answers one.

iss.description: The JWT's issuer, normally '{vendor.app_id}'. May name a vendor value as '{vendor.<key>}' and one of this connection's own fields as '{<key>}'.

key.description: The signing key, as a vendor value: '{vendor.private_key}'. A PEM private key.

lifetime.description: How long the signed JWT lives, in seconds.

webhooks.description: The vendor's webhooks, received by Initiative at one address per plug-in on the deployment, '/api/v1/plugin-hooks/<public_id>'. Initiative checks each delivery's signature, drops one it has already delivered, finds the communities it belongs to by a value in its body, and forwards it to the plug-in's webhook hook once for each. A container plug-in's hook receives each delivery; a declarative plug-in maps it with 'events' and 'status' instead.

dedup.description: The header carrying the vendor's id for one delivery, such as 'X-GitHub-Delivery'. A delivery with an id already forwarded to a community is not forwarded to it again.

events.description: Declarative plug-ins: what a delivery does: emit one of this plug-in's events, change the plug-in's values, or both. The first row whose 'when' holds applies, its 'emit' and its 'write' both; a delivery no row matches is dropped.

status.description: Declarative plug-ins: deliveries that say what state a connection is in at the vendor. The first row whose 'when' holds sets it.

webhookVerify.description: How a delivery's signature is checked: an HMAC over the raw body under a vendor value.

header.description: The header carrying the signature, such as 'X-Hub-Signature-256'.

prefix.description: What precedes the signature in the header, such as 'sha256='. Absent: nothing does.

secret.description: The signing secret, as one vendor value: '{vendor.<key>}'.

webhookRoute.description: Which communities a delivery belongs to: a value in its body or in one of its headers, matched against one field of a static connection as each community's connect stored it. Exactly one of 'path' and 'header'.

path.description: Where the value is in the JSON body, as keys joined by '.', such as 'installation.id'.

header.description: The header carrying the value, such as 'X-Shopify-Shop-Domain'.

connection.description: A static connection this plug-in declares.

field.description: A field that connection declares, whose stored value the body's value is matched against.

schedule.description: Something Initiative runs on an interval, once for each community that installed the plug-in, with when it last succeeded there as 'since'. A container plug-in's schedule calls its schedule hook, and names nothing more. A declarative plug-in's makes one of its read endpoints' calls as the installation and changes the plug-in's values from the answer: it names the 'endpoint' and the 'write', and 'params' when the endpoint takes any.

id.description: Unique within the manifest. A container's hook is told which schedule is due by it. A declarative plug-in's differs from every connection's id: Initiative keys connection health checks by connection id.

every.description: How often: a whole number of minutes ('15m') or hours ('6h'), at least 5 minutes and at most 1440 minutes.

endpoint.description: Declarative plug-ins: a read endpoint this manifest declares, whose 'actors' include 'installation': no person is present when a schedule runs.

params.description: Declarative plug-ins: the endpoint's params, as one expression answering an object. It reads 'since', when the schedule last succeeded in the community (ISO 8601), or null the first time; 'now'; 'connection', the non-secret fields of the connection the endpoint's first request names; 'settings' and 'aliases'. Absent: none.

write.description: Declarative plug-ins: the changes Initiative makes to the plug-in's values from the endpoint's answer, as the install: a list of at most 100 targeted changes ('targetedChange'). It reads 'result', the endpoint's mapped answer, 'since', 'now', 'settings' and 'aliases'. Answering nothing changes nothing.

namespacedId.description: Namespaced under the plug-in's own service id — 'plugin.<public_id>.<name>'. The prefix is checked against the declaring registration at ingress.

pluginScope.description: 'plugins:<public_id>': permission to call another plug-in's public endpoints through the deployment, as this community or as one of its members, and to read the values that plug-in shows on items this one can read. Not one of the fixed scopes: the family is open, one per plug-in, and the public id after the prefix is the plug-in being called. The deployment never lets a plug-in address another directly; the call goes through it, and the plug-in called is handed its own references for whoever the call is for.

label.description: What this endpoint IS, in words somebody picks it out of a list by. Every direction, and an emission most of all: it is the one thing here chosen without ever being called.

description.description: A second line, where the label needs one.

returns.description: What this hands back, by name and type — the response for a read or a write, the payload for an emission. Declared rather than discovered, because a consumer binds one of these before the endpoint has ever run and a bad binding has to be refusable when somebody arranges it.

group.description: Where a consumer that groups a plug-in's endpoints should file this one. Opaque here: the grouping is the consumer's, and an endpoint that says nothing sits in the flat list.

needs_subject.description: What a caller must already have in hand for this to mean anything. Opaque here — the vocabulary belongs to whoever consumes it; the automation service names the subjects a run can be about.

direction.description: 'read' and 'write' are called through the deployment and answer in place; 'emit' travels the other way — the plug-in posts it to a subscriber that registered a URL, so it carries no parameters and nothing to gate.

params.description: What a caller may send. Read and write only.

actors.description: Whose credential the call runs on, best first. Read and write only. An endpoint offering only 'member' refuses when that member has connected nothing, rather than quietly acting as the plug-in instead.

admin_only.description: Only the community's admins read or call this endpoint — a figure for the community's settings page, say. Anyone who can see where it is used may otherwise.

public.description: Read and write only. Other plug-ins may call this endpoint through the deployment, when the community has let them use this plug-in ('plugins:<your public id>'). A caller acts as the community or as one of its members, and `actors` says which of the two this endpoint takes: one that names neither is not callable this way. A write endpoint is reachable only like this; a widget binds reads alone. Absent means only the deployment's own surfaces reach it.

cache_ttl_seconds.description: Read only. How long a response may be reused. Clamped into 0..86400 rather than refused, so a value outside that range is accepted and takes effect at the bound — which is why no range is asserted here.

identity.description: 'write' and 'emit': what this touched, or what it is about. Read endpoints have none — they touched nothing, so there is no echo to suppress.

unavailable.description: Read and write only. The codes this endpoint may answer 'unavailable' with beyond Initiative's own (invalid, mapping-failed, not-authorized, not-found, range-too-large), so a consumer can put each into words.

request.description: Declarative plug-ins: the one call that answers this endpoint. Not beside 'steps'.

steps.description: Declarative plug-ins: up to 3 calls made in order, each able to read the answers of the ones before it. Not beside 'request'.

map.description: Declarative plug-ins: the endpoint's answer, from 'response' (the last call's answer) and 'steps': an object of its declared returns, or {"unavailable": "<code>"} naming one of its codes.

errors.description: Declarative plug-ins: vendor answers this endpoint gives its own meaning, tried on every answer before the defaults. The defaults: 401 and 403 are not-authorized, 404 not-found, 400, 422 and any other 4xx invalid, and 429, 3xx and 5xx transient.

meta.description: The widget's own name and description, as the picker shows them. Must name the widget in at least one language.

module_source.description: The widget's browser-side module. Stored as an opaque string and executed only inside the sandbox; the platform never parses it. Capped in UTF-8 bytes, which this schema cannot express.

endpoints.description: Read endpoint ids this manifest also declares. Only a read answers with something to draw.

sample_data.description: What each endpoint would answer with, keyed by declared read endpoint id, so a preview renders with no network call. Written in the endpoint's own returns and read through them exactly as a live answer is. Keys naming an undeclared endpoint are dropped.

scopes.description: Where the page renders. Declaring both gives it a community-wide entry and an entry inside each initiative.

admin_only.description: Only the community's admins open this page, whatever roles a placement allows — a settings page, say. Who else may open a page is chosen in the community, per initiative and per role, not declared here.

capabilities.description: Browser features the frame is granted. A page that names nothing is framed with all of them denied.

metadataKey.description: A key the plug-in keeps a value under, on an item or on its own install: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits, '_' and '.'.

field.description: How one of the plug-in's metadata keys is shown on Initiative's items. The value is kept in Initiative: a container plug-in writes it with its installation token, and for a declarative plug-in Initiative writes it from the plug-in's expressions. Initiative draws it with its own component for `kind` and computes its plain text itself, so a field filters, sorts and exports with no call to the plug-in. Which views show it is chosen by the community's managers, never by the plug-in. Initiative holds what is kept, and these caps are enforced there rather than here: a value of at most 8192 bytes as JSON, with a string of at most 255 characters to be found by, and each element of a list a value of its own, found by its 'ref'; at most 32 keys and 65536 bytes on one item, and 256 keys and 1048576 bytes on the install.

key.description: The metadata key whose value this shows. Unique among this manifest's fields.

kind.description: What the value is, and so how it is drawn: 'text' a string; 'number' a number; 'date' a 'YYYY-MM-DD' string; 'datetime' an ISO 8601 string with its offset; 'link' {url, text?}; 'badge' {text, tone?}; 'progress' {value, max}; 'checkbox' a boolean.

list.description: Several values rather than one: the value is a list of elements, each one value of 'kind' with a 'ref' that tells it from the others ('listElement'). A change gives the whole list in 'set', or adds, replaces and removes elements by 'ref' with 'upsert' and 'remove'. Absent: one value, which a change sets.

on.description: The item kinds it is offered on.

description.description: The one line the view editor's Add picker shows beside the name.

tone.description: A badge's tone when its value names none.

states.description: What state the value is in, as facets by id, at most 4, each with keys of its own. The value names a key of each facet it is in as 'state', {"<facet>": "<key>"}, and Initiative draws each as a badge, labelled in the reader's language. A list element, and a link, badge or progress value, carries 'state' beside its other properties; a text, number, date, datetime or checkbox value that carries one is written as an element is, without the 'ref': {"value": …, "state": …}.

actions.description: Declarative plug-ins, on a list field: actions offered on each of its elements, by id, each one offered on every item kind this field is. An action run from an element reads that element's 'ref' as 'element'.

stateFacet.description: One facet of a field's state, such as whether a piece of work is open or what review it has: its name, and the keys a value may name.

values.description: The keys a value may name, at most 12, each with its badge's words and tone.

stateValue.description: One key of a state facet, as its badge shows it.

partNode.description: One node of a part: one of Initiative's own components, told apart by 'type', with its props and, for a section or a stack, the nodes inside it.

sectionNode.description: A titled group, which the reader may fold.

collapsed.description: Drawn folded until the reader opens it.

children.description: Drawn in order, inside this one.

stackNode.description: Nodes side by side or one above another.

gap.description: The space between the nodes. Absent: Initiative's own.

wrap.description: A row runs onto a second line rather than past its edge.

children.description: Drawn in order, inside this one.

fieldNode.description: A field's label and its value.

field.description: One of this manifest's fields, by its key, offered on every item kind the part is.
One of this manifest's fields, by its key, offered on every item kind the part is.

text.description: May name '{item.id}', the item's id, and '{settings.<key>}', one of this plug-in's settings, which Initiative fills in when it draws the part. Any other '{…}' is refused.

buttonNode.description: A button that runs one of this plug-in's actions on the item, labelled with the action's name.

action.description: One of this manifest's actions, by its id, offered on every item kind the part is.

part.description: A piece of an item's page or view, built from Initiative's own components and bound to this plug-in's fields and actions. Data only: Initiative draws each node, and no plug-in code runs in the reader's browser. Which views show it is chosen by the community's managers, never by the plug-in, and Initiative places at most 3 of a plug-in's parts on one item.

name.description: What the view editor calls it.

on.description: The item kinds it is offered on.

tree.description: What is drawn: at most 50 nodes, at most 4 deep.

description.description: The one line the view editor's Add picker shows beside the name.

action.description: Something a reader runs on one item, from a part's button, the item's own menu, or an element of a list field that offers it. Initiative first asks the reader for the 'params' the action names, when it names any. For a container plug-in, Initiative only connects: it calls the write endpoint as the installation, with those parameters, the reader as 'viewer' and the item as 'subject' in the call's token, and the endpoint does the work, usually writing the plug-in's metadata. For a declarative plug-in, Initiative does the work: it makes the endpoint's call, when the action names one, with those parameters, on the credential its 'actors' say, its expressions reading the item as 'item' and the element it was run from, if any, as 'element'; then it makes the change 'write' answers, when the action has one, to the plug-in's values on the item, as the install. Either way Initiative then answers the reader with the item's metadata as it stands.

name.description: The button's or the menu entry's label.

endpoint.description: An endpoint this manifest declares. A container plug-in's action names a write, which its handler answers. A declarative plug-in's names a read or a write, a 'write' expression, or both: a read fetches what the 'write' keeps, a write changes something at the vendor.

params.description: Parameters of the action's endpoint, by key, that Initiative asks the reader for before it runs the action, in a form drawn from the endpoint's own declarations of them: each one's type and label, and its 'options' or 'options_from'. The endpoint is sent these and nothing else, so every parameter it requires is among them.

write.description: Declarative plug-ins: the change Initiative makes to the plug-in's values on the action's item, as the install: one change ('change'). It reads 'item', the item ({kind, id, title}); 'held', this install's values on it, by key; 'result', the endpoint's mapped answer, absent when the action names no endpoint; 'params', what the reader answered; 'element', the 'ref' of the list element it was run from, absent when it was not; 'settings', 'aliases' and 'now'. Answering nothing changes nothing.

on.description: The item kinds it is offered on.

confirm.description: A question Initiative asks before running it. Absent: it runs at once.

menu.description: Also offered in the item's own menu.

admin_only.description: Only the community's admins run this action, whatever roles a placement allows. Who else may run it is chosen in the community, per initiative and per role, not declared here.

change.description: A change to the plug-in's values on one item or on its install, as a declarative plug-in's 'write' answers it. 'set' writes values by key, as a container's client.metadata.set does; 'upsert' and 'remove' change a list field's elements by their 'ref'. A change gives at least one of the three, and changes each key with only one. Initiative makes it as the install, and holds what is kept to the caps a field's description gives.

set.description: Values by metadata key, each any JSON value of at most 8192 bytes; a null removes its key. A list field's value is its whole list of elements, each held to that cap.

upsert.description: Elements by metadata key ('listElement'): each is added to that key's list, or merged into the element there with its 'ref': the properties it gives replace that element's, the ones it leaves out stay, and its 'state' merges the same way by facet. So a write that knows one fact about an element changes that fact alone.

remove.description: Refs by metadata key: the element with each is taken from that key's list. A ref the list does not hold changes nothing.

targetedChange.description: A change and where Initiative makes it. A webhook event's or a schedule's 'write' answers a list of at most 100, and cannot read what their targets hold.

set.description: As a change's: values by metadata key, a null removing its key.

upsert.description: As a change's: elements by metadata key, each added to its list or merged into the one with its 'ref', property by property and its 'state' facet by facet.

remove.description: As a change's: refs by metadata key, each element with one taken from its list.

changeTarget.description: Where a change is made: {kind, id}, one item; {install: true}, the install itself; or {holding: {key, value}}, every item on which this install holds 'value' under 'key', as a container's client.metadata.find finds them. Initiative keeps each element of a list as a value of its own, so 'holding' reaches an element by its 'ref'. A target the install cannot read is skipped.

value.description: A value is found by its text: a string as it is, a number or a boolean as JSON writes it; a list element by its 'ref'.

listElement.description: One element of a list field's value: one value of the field's 'kind', with a 'ref' that tells it from the list's others. A text, number, date, datetime or checkbox element holds its value in 'value'; a link element is {ref, url, text?}, a badge element {ref, text, tone?} and a progress element {ref, value, max}. Initiative keeps each element as a value of its own, of at most 8192 bytes as JSON. An 'upsert' may give only some of an element's properties: they are merged into the element with its 'ref'.

value.description: A text, number, date, datetime or checkbox element's value, or a progress element's figure.

text.description: A link element's words, or a badge element's.

state.description: A key of each of the field's state facets this element is in, by facet id.

elementRef.description: What tells a list's element from the others, such as the vendor's own id for what it shows: unique in its list, and how a change replaces or removes the element and a 'holding' target finds it.

setting.description: A value the community's admins see and may change on the install, which the plug-in's expressions read as 'settings.<key>' and its parts' text names as '{settings.<key>}'.

type.description: What the value is: 'string', a line of text.

unique.description: No two communities on a deployment hold the same value for this plug-in, and the value is a 'uniqueSettingValue'. An admin who renames it keeps the earlier values, which no other community may take and the plug-in's expressions read as 'aliases.<key>'.

assigned.description: A unique setting's only: Initiative gives it a value when the community installs the plug-in, which an admin may rename. 'community_name': the letters and digits of the community's name, in lowercase, with a short random suffix when another community holds that value.

uniqueSettingValue.description: A unique setting's value: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters and digits, two to 16 characters in all. It holds no '-', so a reference such as '<value>-<number>' reads one way.

uid.description: This dashboard's own catalog id — publisher-assigned, immutable, never reused. It becomes a listing of its own, so this is a real catalog identity and not the plug-in's.

public_id.description: '<publisher>.<slug>', and not the plug-in's own — a bundled dashboard is a separate listing.

type.description: One of this manifest's own widget ids — bare, with no uid. The platform stamps the plug-in's uid on when it publishes, so the two can never disagree.

endpoint_id.description: One of this manifest's own read endpoint ids. Only a read answers with something to draw.

endpointIdentity.description: Which of this endpoint's returns identify the thing it touched. A consumer keeps a change an automation made from firing that automation again, and for a plug-in there was no key — so guessing would silently drop a fire somebody was waiting on, and a rate cap was the only guard. Declare the SAME kind and key on the write and on the emission about it, and the two produce the same address.

kind.description: Your own word for what sort of thing this is ('issue'). Namespaced by your public id downstream, because two plug-ins declaring the same kind mean two different things.

key.description: Returns of this endpoint, in order, joined to form the address. Every one must be a single value rather than a list — half an address matches nothing, and one built from the parts that happened to be there matches the wrong thing.

expression.description: A JSONata expression (https://jsonata.org): standard JSONata, with no functions added. It reads one document. On the way out that holds 'params', the call's parameters as the caller sent them; 'connection', the non-secret fields of the connection the request names; 'connections', on an endpoint's requests and map, each connection its 'requires' names that the call has, by its id, holding the same fields; 'now', the time of the call in ISO 8601, which $now() and $millis() also answer; 'steps', each earlier step's answer by its name; and, on the call an action makes, 'item', the item it runs on: {kind, id, title}, and 'element', the 'ref' of the list element it was run from, if it was. On the way back it also holds 'response', the answer being read: {status, headers, body}, with header names in lowercase. Every expression of a declarative plug-in also reads 'settings', the install's settings by key, and 'aliases', each unique setting's earlier values by key, as a list, except a token's 'exchange_body', which reads only its connection. Each evaluation is bounded: at most 1000 milliseconds, 500 levels of nesting and an answer of 1048576 bytes as JSON. An expression that fails or passes a bound answers 'unavailable: mapping-failed'.

host.description: A host a declarative plug-in calls, in lowercase: exact ('api.github.com'), or with one leading '*.' that stands for exactly one label ('*.myshopify.com'). No scheme, port or path: every call is https on port 443, and goes only to a public address.

vendorAuth.description: How Initiative puts a connection's credential on a declarative plug-in's requests: one header, holding the prefix and the token joined by a space. Absent: 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'.

prefix.description: Written before the token. Empty: the token alone.

vendorRequest.description: One call Initiative makes to the vendor for a declarative plug-in, rendered from expressions. Initiative adds the credential itself, as 'auth' says, and follows no redirect.

url.description: The address, as an expression answering a string: https, on one of the plug-in's hosts. Query parameters may be written into it or given in 'query'.

query.description: Query parameters by name, each an expression. One answering null or nothing is left out, and a list repeats the parameter once per value.

headers.description: Headers by name, each an expression answering a string; one answering null or nothing is left out. Never the credential's header, which Initiative sets.

body.description: The JSON body, as an expression. Not beside 'graphql'.

connection.description: Which connection's credential the request carries: one connection for every call, or, on a write endpoint's requests, one per actor ('actorConnections'), so a call made as the member carries the member's own credential and one made as the installation the community's. A static connection's credential is the community's, an interactive one's the acting member's, which a call made as the installation does not have. A call made as a member carries a static connection's credential only when the endpoint's 'requires' names that connection, and is refused otherwise. Required on an endpoint's requests. Absent on 'after_connect' and 'health', which carry the credential of the connection they belong to.

graphqlRequest.description: A GraphQL request, sent by POST as the JSON body {query, variables}.

query.description: The GraphQL document, as text. What varies goes in 'variables'.

variables.description: The variables, as an expression answering an object.

actorConnections.description: One connection per actor, on a write endpoint's requests: a call carries the credential of the connection named for the actor it is made as. Names exactly the actors the endpoint's 'actors' declare. The member's connection need not be named in 'requires': a call made as the member requires the connection its requests name for the member.

member.description: An interactive connection, which a call made as the member carries: the member's own account.

installation.description: A static connection, which a call made as the installation carries: the community's own.

name.description: Unique among its steps. Later steps, the map and the predicates beside it read this step's answer as 'steps.<name>'.

paging.description: How a request reads more than one page, one member per method, told apart by 'kind'. Every page is read before the answer is mapped: 'response.body' is then every page's items appended in order, and the status and headers are the last page's. 'max_pages' is how many pages may be read; finding more after that many truncates or refuses, as 'on_limit' says, and a refusal answers 'unavailable: range-too-large'.

pageNumberPaging.description: Numbered pages from 1, read until one holds fewer than 'per_page' items. Both parameters are added to the request's query.

page_param.description: The parameter carrying the page number.

per_page_param.description: The parameter carrying 'per_page'. Absent: the vendor's page size is fixed, and 'per_page' says what it is.

linkHeaderPaging.description: The address in the Link header's rel="next", followed until there is none. It must be https on one of the plug-in's hosts.

cursorPaging.description: A cursor read from each page and sent with the next, while 'more' holds. Exactly one of 'param' and 'variable' says where it is sent.

next.description: The next page's cursor, from this page's 'response'.

more.description: Whether there is a next page, from this page's 'response'.

param.description: The query parameter the cursor is sent in.

variable.description: The GraphQL variable the cursor is sent in.

pageItems.description: A page's items, from that page's 'response'. Absent: its body.

statusMatch.description: An HTTP status: one code, or a range of a hundred ('4xx').

errorRule.description: A vendor answer an endpoint gives its own meaning. Rules are tried in order on every answer, a 2xx included, and the first that matches decides.

when.description: Also required to hold, over the answer as 'response'. Absent: the status alone matches.

code.description: What the call answers: one of the endpoint's 'unavailable' codes, one of Initiative's own (invalid, mapping-failed, not-authorized, not-found, range-too-large), or 'transient' for a passing failure such as a throttle, which is answered as one to retry.

afterConnect.description: A declarative plug-in's after_connect: a request, or up to 3 steps, made with the access token just obtained, and the answers mapped to what the hook would answer. 'params' holds the flow's own parameters, such as the installation_id an install page returned.

steps.description: Up to 3 calls made in order, each able to read the answers of the ones before it. Not beside 'request'.

map.description: The connection's managed values and its account label, from 'response' (the last call's answer) and 'steps': {"values": {…}, "account_label": "…"}.

refuse_when.description: Refuses the connection when it holds. It reads the map's answer as 'result', beside 'response' and 'steps'.

code.description: What a refusal answers. Given exactly when 'refuse_when' is.

connectionHealth.description: Declarative plug-ins: a request Initiative makes on an interval, with this connection's credential, to learn whether the connection still works. A state other than 'ok' is reported once two answers in a row give it.

every.description: How often: a whole number of minutes ('15m') or hours ('6h'), at least 5 minutes and at most 1440 minutes.

states.description: Tried in order; the first that matches gives the state. An answer none matches is 'ok' when it is 2xx and 'unavailable' otherwise.

healthState.description: The answers one row matches, and the state they mean. A row naming neither 'status' nor 'when' matches any answer.

when.description: Also required to hold, over the answer as 'response'.

webhookEvent.description: What one kind of delivery does: emit an event, change the plug-in's values, or both. It gives 'emit', 'write' or both, and 'map' exactly when it gives 'emit'. Its expressions read 'headers' (names in lowercase), 'payload' (the parsed body), 'connection' (the routed connection's non-secret fields), 'now', 'settings' and 'aliases'.

emit.description: An emit endpoint this manifest declares.

map.description: The event's payload: an object of that endpoint's declared returns.

write.description: The changes Initiative makes to the plug-in's values, as the install: a list of at most 100 targeted changes ('targetedChange'). Answering nothing changes nothing.

webhookStatus.description: A delivery that says what state a connection is in, read as an event's expressions are.
